title: Composite vs porcelain vs Lumineers: which veneer is right for you?
seoTitle: Composite vs Porcelain Veneers vs Lumineers: Cost, Lifespan, Prep
description: Composite, porcelain and Lumineers compared on cost per tooth, visits, enamel removed, how long each lasts and cost per year, plus who is really a no-prep candidate.
author: Dr. Gretell Alonso Fiel, DMD
imageAlt: Ultra-thin porcelain veneer held with tweezers
answer: Composite veneers cost about **$250 to $1,500 per tooth**, take one visit and last **5 to 7 years**. Porcelain veneers cost **$900 to $2,500 per tooth** at most practices, need two visits and last **10 to 15 years** or longer. Lumineers are a brand of thin porcelain veneer bonded with little or no drilling, and they suit some teeth and not others. At Xiluet Smiles, 20 porcelain veneers at 0.3 mm cost **$6,000**.

blocks.p: All three are shells bonded to the front of your teeth. The differences are the material, how much tooth is removed to make room for it, how long it lasts, and what it costs you per year rather than per visit. This table is the summary. The sections below give the detail and the sources.

blocks.p: Per-tooth ranges and lifespans come from [Cleveland Clinic](https://my.clevelandclinic.org/health/treatments/23522-dental-veneers) and a [2026 US cost comparison](https://realdentalcosts.com/en/veneers-cost-porcelain-vs-composite/). Lumineers are porcelain, so most practices price them like their other porcelain veneers; ask for the number in writing.

sections.h2: Composite veneers: fast, cheap, and temporary

blocks.p: Composite is the same resin used for white fillings. The dentist builds it onto the tooth by hand, shapes it and polishes it in the chair, so you leave with the result the same day. Nothing goes to a lab. That is why it is cheap: $250 to $1,500 per tooth nationally, and Miami practices published composite sets for 20 teeth from about $3,000 to $6,000 in October 2026.

The trade-off is the material. Resin is softer than porcelain and slightly porous. It picks up coffee, wine and tobacco stains, loses its polish, and chips at the edges. Cleveland Clinic gives 5 to 7 years as the usual lifespan, and that assumes you keep up with polishing visits. The real advantage is that a chip can be patched in the chair in minutes, with no lab.

list: **Composite makes sense when:** one tooth is chipped, you want to test a new shape before committing to porcelain, or the budget today matters more than the cost over ten years.

**Composite struggles when:** the teeth are dark (tetracycline, fluorosis), because resin thick enough to hide the stain looks flat and opaque; or you want 20 teeth, because hand-building 20 veneers is many hours in the chair and the set will need redoing roughly twice in the time one porcelain set lasts.

blocks.p: Porcelain veneers are made in a lab from a scan of your teeth, then bonded. That means two visits at most practices, or three visits in one week at Xiluet, where the lab is in the building. Nationally they run $900 to $2,500 per tooth; the 2026 Synchrony study cited by [CareCredit](https://www.carecredit.com/well-u/health-wellness/dental-veneers-cost-dental-veneers-financing/) puts the average single porcelain veneer at about $1,455. Miami ranges are in our [cost guide](/blog/porcelain-veneers-cost-miami).

The lifespan numbers are better documented than for any other veneer. A [pooled analysis of about 6,500 porcelain veneers](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7961608/) found 95.5% still in place at 10 years, and single studies report 91% at 20 years. When they do fail, it is usually a fracture or a debond, most often in the first two years. Porcelain does not stain and keeps its gloss. It also does not bleach, so you choose the shade once, and we match it in person.

Preparation is where porcelain earns its reputation, good and bad. A well-planned porcelain veneer removes 0.3 to 0.7 mm from the front of the tooth and stays in enamel. A [15-year study of 672 veneers](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/jerd.70016) found 96.7% survival when the veneer was bonded to enamel against 93.9% when more than 30% of the surface was dentin, and dentin exposure raised the odds of failure 3.5 times. The brand matters less than the millimetres. More on that in [do veneers ruin your teeth](/blog/do-veneers-ruin-your-teeth).

sections.h2: Lumineers and no-prep veneers: who is actually a candidate

blocks.p: Lumineers is a brand name for a very thin porcelain veneer made by one laboratory and bonded with little or no drilling. "No-prep" is the general term for the same idea. The appeal is obvious: enamel untouched, no temporaries, and a result that is closer to reversible than a prepared veneer, although removing bonded porcelain is never simple.

The catch is physics. A veneer adds thickness. If nothing is removed, the tooth gets bigger by the thickness of the shell. On teeth that are small, worn short, set back or spaced, that extra volume is exactly what you want. On teeth that are already full-size, crowded or tipped outward, it makes them look bulky and leaves a ledge at the gum line that traps plaque and inflames the gum, which [Healthline](https://www.healthline.com/health/dental-veneers) lists as the usual complaint. And because the shell is so thin, it hides less: dark teeth show through.

list: **Good no-prep candidates:** small or peg-shaped teeth, gaps, teeth worn short by grinding, teeth tipped slightly inward, a mild color change.
**Usually need some preparation:** crowding or rotation, teeth that already protrude, very dark teeth, old bonding or large fillings on the front surface.

blocks.p: In practice, no-prep is not a decision you make from a website. It is made tooth by tooth from the scans. In many sets, some teeth are no-prep and their neighbours need 0.3 mm. That is normal, and a doctor who tells you every tooth will be no-prep before seeing you is guessing.

sections.h2: Cost per year, not cost per visit

blocks.p: The cheapest veneer is the one you replace least often. Divide the price by the years it is expected to last and the picture changes. The ranges below were published by Miami practices in October 2026; they change, so treat them as a guide.

Composite also needs polishing and patch repairs along the way, which are not in the table. Porcelain usually needs nothing, and ours carries a 5-year written warranty. So composite's honest advantage is the price today, not the price over time. If today's price is the constraint, [financing](/financing) spreads $6,000 over monthly payments; as an example, 48 months at 9% APR is about $149 a month, with terms set by the lender and subject to approval.

We do not sell a brand. Our veneers are porcelain, hand-finished by a ceramist in our building, and 0.3 mm thick where the case allows. At Visit 1 your doctor reviews the scans and tells you, tooth by tooth, whether any enamel needs removing: often very little, sometimes none. You see the design in your mouth and approve it before any tooth is touched. Shade is matched in person with the ceramist, not from a photo sent to another city.

[20 porcelain veneers cost $6,000](/porcelain-veneers-miami). That includes the professional cleaning and X-rays, the design preview, temporaries shaped like your final design, delivery in 5 business days and a 5-year warranty in writing. Three visits in one week. Prices shown are minimum fees; your final fee is confirmed in writing after a doctor's evaluation. If you grind, we will ask you to wear a night guard.

blocks.quote: The question is never composite, porcelain or a brand name. It is how much tooth has to go, and whether the result will still look right in ten years.

steps: **Send photos first.** Three photos through the [free photo evaluation](/free-photo-evaluation) and a doctor replies within 6 hours with a written estimate and an opinion on which option fits your teeth.
**Ask how much tooth will be removed, in millimetres, for each tooth.** Any practice selling porcelain or no-prep veneers should be able to answer after scans.
**Ask for the lifespan and the warranty in writing.** Five to seven years for composite, ten or more for porcelain. A warranty that is not written down is not a warranty.
**Ask to see the design before any drilling.** For porcelain and no-prep alike. For composite, ask the dentist to build one tooth first and show you.
**Divide the price by the years.** Then decide.

faq.q: Are Lumineers better than porcelain veneers?
faq.a: Lumineers are porcelain veneers from one brand, made very thin so little or no tooth is removed. They are neither better nor worse. They suit small, spaced or set-back teeth and suit crowded, protruding or dark teeth poorly. Your scans decide, tooth by tooth.

faq.q: How long do composite veneers last?
faq.a: Usually 5 to 7 years. They stain and chip sooner than porcelain, but a chip can be patched in the chair without a lab.

faq.q: Can I switch from composite to porcelain later?
faq.a: Yes. The composite is removed, the tooth is scanned and prepared minimally, and a porcelain veneer is made. Many patients who start with composite on several teeth do this once the resin starts to stain.

faq.q: Do no-prep veneers come off more easily?
faq.a: No. Untouched enamel is the best surface there is for bonding porcelain. The problems with no-prep veneers come from bulk at the gum line on the wrong teeth, not from the bond.

faq.q: Does Xiluet place Lumineers or composite veneers?
faq.a: Our packages are porcelain: 20 veneers at 0.3 mm for $6,000, made in our own lab. If a tooth suits no-prep, your doctor tells you at Visit 1 and bonds the veneer without drilling. If you only need a single chipped tooth repaired, say so when you send photos and we will quote the right option in writing.
